---
title: "Baseline"
---

The chapter 10 calculators as they are now: the `{ojs}` code cells of
[chapter 10](https://trustworthyresear.ch/chapters/10_recalculation_methods.html)
of Ian Hussey's book (code: MIT licence), copied unchanged by `R/get_baseline.R`
from commit `e754f2b` of the `dev` branch.

#### statcheck {#sec-statcheck-app}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof scBatch = {
  const examples = [
    "t(58) = 1.46, p = .03",
    "t(28) = 2.0, p < .05",
    "F(1, 7) = 12.19, p < .001",
    "χ2(1, N = 226) = 6.90, p < .01",
    "r(40) = −.30, p = .03",
    "t(30) = 2.10, p = .000",
    "F(2, 70) = 4.48, MSE = 6.61, p < .02"
  ]
  const text = html`<textarea class="form-control sc-batch" rows="8" spellcheck="false" aria-label="Results to check, one per line"></textarea>`
  text.value = examples.join("\n")
  const oneTailed = html`<input type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" id="sc-one-tailed">`
  const run = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Run statcheck</button>`
  const clear = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Clear</button>`
  const view = html`<div>
    <label class="sc-label">Results to check, one per line</label>
    ${text}
    <div class="form-check sc-option">${oneTailed}<label class="form-check-label" for="sc-one-tailed">Treat all tests as one-sided (<code>OneTailedTests = TRUE</code>)</label></div>
    <div class="sb-buttons">${run}${clear}</div>
  </div>`
  // the value only changes when the button is clicked, so that statcheck is not run on every keystroke
  view.value = {runs: 0}
  run.onclick = () => {
    view.value = {runs: view.value.runs + 1, text: text.value, oneTailed: oneTailed.checked}
    view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  }
  clear.onclick = () => { text.value = ""; text.focus() }
  return view
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  if (scBatch.runs === 0) {
    yield html`<div class="sc-status">Click <strong>Run statcheck</strong> to check the results above.</div>`
    return
  }
  // blank lines are left out, and each remaining line keeps its number, so that results can be matched to lines
  const lines = scBatch.text.split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.trim()).filter(l => l.length > 0)
  if (lines.length === 0) {
    yield html`<div class="sc-status">Paste at least one result into the box.</div>`
    return
  }
  yield html`<div class="sc-status"><span class="spinner-border spinner-border-sm" role="status"></span> ${statcheckR.started() ? "Running statcheck…" : "Starting R in your browser and installing statcheck. This takes several seconds the first time…"}</div>`
  yield runStatcheck(lines, scBatch.oneTailed).then(statcheckTable, e => html`<div class="sb-feedback sb-feedback-bad"><strong>Something went wrong.</strong> ${e.message}</div>`)
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// functions and styles used by the statcheck app

// webR, a version of R compiled to WebAssembly, is only downloaded and started the first time it is needed, and is
// then shared by the statcheck app and the SMD calculator. each R package is installed the first time it is needed.
// the webR version is pinned, so that the versions of R and of the packages do not change unnoticed
webrVersion = "0.6.0"

webRSession = {
  let session = null
  const packages = new Map()
  const startR = async () => {
    const {WebR} = await import(`https://webr.r-wasm.org/v${webrVersion}/webr.mjs`)
    const webR = new WebR()
    await webR.init()
    return {webR, rVersion: await webR.evalRString("R.version.string")}
  }
  // if starting R or installing a package fails, the next click tries again
  const getR = () => session ??= startR().catch(e => { session = null; throw e })
  const install = async pkg => {
    const {webR, rVersion} = await getR()
    await webR.installPackages([pkg], {quiet: true})
    await webR.evalRVoid(`suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(${pkg}))`)
    return {webR, rVersion, version: await webR.evalRString(`as.character(packageVersion("${pkg}"))`)}
  }
  return {
    // whether a package has been requested, so that the first, slower run can say what it is doing
    started: pkg => packages.has(pkg),
    load: pkg => {
      if (!packages.has(pkg)) packages.set(pkg, install(pkg).catch(e => { packages.delete(pkg); throw e }))
      return packages.get(pkg)
    }
  }
}

statcheckR = ({
  started: () => webRSession.started("statcheck"),
  get: () => webRSession.load("statcheck").then(({webR, rVersion, version}) =>
    ({webR, rVersion, statcheckVersion: version, version: `statcheck ${version}, ${rVersion}, running in webR ${webrVersion}`}))
})

async function runStatcheck(lines, oneTailed) {
  const {webR, ...versions} = await statcheckR.get()
  const shelter = await new webR.Shelter()
  try {
    // the lines are passed to R as a character vector, never pasted into the code, and named by their line number
    // so that each result statcheck returns can be matched to the line it came from
    const res = await shelter.evalR(`
      names(lines) <- seq_along(lines)
      res <- statcheck(lines, OneTailedTests = one_tailed, messages = FALSE)
      if (is.null(res)) data.frame() else as.data.frame(res)
    `, {env: {lines, one_tailed: oneTailed}})
    const rows = await res.toD3()
    return {lines, rows, oneTailed, runAt: new Date(), ...versions}
  } finally {
    shelter.purge()
  }
}

function statcheckTable(run) {
  const {lines, rows, version, oneTailed} = run
  // one row per result found, and one per line in which statcheck found no result
  const verdict = r => r.error === null ? ["Could not check", "na"]
    : r.decision_error ? ["Grossly inconsistent", "bad"]
    : r.error ? ["Inconsistent", "warn"]
    : ["Consistent", "ok"]
  const comparison = r => r.p_comp === "ns" ? "ns" : `p ${r.p_comp} ${formatReported(r)}`
  const body = lines.flatMap((line, i) => {
    const found = rows.filter(r => r.source === String(i + 1))
    if (found.length === 0) return [html`<tr class="sc-row-none"><td>${i + 1}</td><td>${line}</td><td></td><td></td><td>Not recognised</td></tr>`]
    return found.map(r => {
      const [label, kind] = verdict(r)
      return html`<tr><td>${i + 1}</td><td>${r.raw}</td><td>${comparison(r)}</td><td>${r.computed_p === null ? "" : formatP(r.computed_p)}</td><td><span class="sc-verdict sc-verdict-${kind}">${label}</span></td></tr>`
    })
  })
  const counts = d3.rollup(rows, v => v.length, r => verdict(r)[0])
  const summary = ["Consistent", "Inconsistent", "Grossly inconsistent"].map(k => `${counts.get(k) ?? 0} ${k.toLowerCase()}`).join(", ")
  const unread = lines.filter((l, i) => !rows.some(r => r.source === String(i + 1))).length
  return html`<div>
    <div class="table-responsive"><table class="table table-sm sc-table">
      <thead><tr><th>Line</th><th>Result as read by statcheck</th><th>Reported</th><th>Recalculated <em>p</em></th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>${body}</tbody>
    </table></div>
    <div class="sc-status">${rows.length} result${rows.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} found: ${summary}.${unread > 0 ? ` ${unread} line${unread === 1 ? " was" : "s were"} not recognised.` : ""} Tests treated as ${oneTailed ? "one-sided" : "two-sided"}, with α = .05. ${version}.</div>
    <div class="sb-buttons sc-download">${downloadButton(run, verdict)}</div>
  </div>`
}

function downloadButton(run, verdict) {
  // a button that saves the inputs, statcheck's output, and the versions used as a CSV file. one row per result found,
  // and one per line in which statcheck found no result, in the same order as the table
  const {lines, rows, oneTailed, runAt, statcheckVersion, rVersion} = run
  const columns = ["line", "input", "raw", "test_type", "df1", "df2", "test_comp", "test_value", "p_comp", "reported_p", "computed_p", "error", "decision_error", "verdict",
    "one_tailed_tests", "alpha", "statcheck_version", "r_version", "webr_version", "run_at"]
  const settings = {one_tailed_tests: oneTailed, alpha: 0.05, statcheck_version: statcheckVersion, r_version: rVersion, webr_version: webrVersion, run_at: runAt.toISOString()}
  const records = lines.flatMap((line, i) => {
    const found = rows.filter(r => r.source === String(i + 1))
    if (found.length === 0) return [{line: i + 1, input: line, verdict: "Not recognised", ...settings}]
    // the reported p-value is kept as it was written, so that its decimals are not lost
    return found.map(r => ({...r, line: i + 1, input: line, reported_p: r.p_comp === "ns" ? "" : formatReported(r), verdict: verdict(r)[0], ...settings}))
  })
  return csvDownloadButton(columns, records, "statcheck_results", runAt)
}

function csvDownloadButton(columns, records, prefix, runAt) {
  // a button that saves records (objects with the given columns) as a CSV file, named after the prefix and the local
  // date and time of the run, e.g. statcheck_results_2026-10-16_14-05-09.csv
  const cell = x => {
    if (x === null || x === undefined) return ""
    const text = typeof x === "boolean" ? (x ? "TRUE" : "FALSE") : String(x)
    return /[",\n\r]/.test(text) ? `"${text.replace(/"/g, '""')}"` : text
  }
  const csv = [columns.join(","), ...records.map(r => columns.map(c => cell(r[c])).join(","))].join("\r\n")
  const pad = n => String(n).padStart(2, "0")
  const d = runAt
  const name = `${prefix}_${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}_${pad(d.getHours())}-${pad(d.getMinutes())}-${pad(d.getSeconds())}.csv`
  const button = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Download results as CSV</button>`
  button.onclick = () => {
    // the byte order mark lets spreadsheet programs read symbols such as χ and − correctly
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob(["\ufeff" + csv], {type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8"}))
    const link = html`<a href="${url}" download="${name}"></a>`
    document.body.append(link)
    link.click()
    link.remove()
    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000)
  }
  return button
}

function formatReported(r) {
  // the reported p-value as it was written, so that its decimals are kept (statcheck returns it as a number, in which
  // .000 becomes 0 and .040 becomes 0.04). falls back to the number, without its leading zero
  const written = r.raw.match(/p\s*[=<>]\s*(0?\.\d+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$/i)
  return written ? written[1] : String(r.reported_p).replace(/^0\./, ".")
}

statcheckAppStyle = html`<style>
  .sc-batch { font-family: var(--bs-font-monospace); font-size: 0.9rem; }
  .sc-option { margin: 0.5rem 0; }
  .sc-download { margin-bottom: 1.5rem; }
  .sc-status { margin: 0.75rem 0 1.5rem; color: var(--bs-secondary-color); font-size: 0.9rem; }
  .sc-table { font-size: 0.9rem; margin-top: 0.75rem; }
  .sc-table td:nth-child(2) { font-family: var(--bs-font-monospace); font-size: 0.85rem; }
  .sc-row-none td { color: var(--bs-secondary-color); }
  .sc-verdict { display: inline-block; padding: 0.1rem 0.5rem; border-left: 4px solid; background: rgba(128, 128, 128, 0.08); white-space: nowrap; }
  .sc-verdict-ok { border-color: #3b9c6e; }
  .sc-verdict-warn { border-color: #d9a02b; }
  .sc-verdict-bad { border-color: #c0392b; }
  .sc-verdict-na { border-color: #8a8a8a; }
</style>`
```

#### Rounding: statcheck checks an interval, not a value {#sec-statcheck-rounding}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof scText = resultInput([
  "t(58) = 1.46, p = .03",
  "t(28) = 2.0, p < .05",
  "r(40) = .3, p = .03",
  "t(40) = 1.80, p = .040",
  "F(2, 40) = 3.50, p = .067",
  "χ2(1, N = 226) = 6.90, p < .01"
], "t(28) = 2.0, p < .05")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof scTwoTailed = toggleButton([{label: "Two-sided test", value: true}, {label: "One-sided test", value: false}])
viewof scRounding = toggleButton([{label: "Rounding accounted for", value: true}, {label: "Rounding ignored", value: false}])
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
scState = {
  const parsed = parseResult(scText)
  if (parsed.message) return parsed
  const {type, stat, df1, df2, statDec, pComp, pRep, pDec} = parsed
  // t, r, and z tests can be one-sided. F and chi-squared tests are one-sided by construction
  const sidedApplies = type === "t" || type === "r" || type === "z"
  const twoTailed = sidedApplies ? scTwoTailed : true
  const pOf = x => pFrom(type, x, df1, df2, twoTailed)
  // the p-values of t, r, and z tests depend only on the size of the statistic, not its sign
  const mag = sidedApplies ? Math.abs(stat) : stat
  // the range of values that round to the reported test statistic, as in statcheck: plus and minus half a unit of
  // its last reported decimal. a larger statistic gives a smaller p-value, so the upper bound of the statistic gives
  // the lower bound of the p-value
  const step = 1 / 10 ** statDec
  const half = scRounding ? step / 2 : 0
  const lowStat = Math.max(0, mag - half), upStat = type === "r" ? Math.min(1 - 1e-12, mag + half) : mag + half
  const computed = pOf(mag), upP = pOf(lowStat), lowP = pOf(upStat)
  // statcheck's decision rules, for a test statistic reported with "=" and alpha = .05. an exact reported p-value is
  // compared with the bounds rounded to its own number of decimals. a p-value of exactly zero is always an error
  const round = (x, d) => Math.round(x * 10 ** d) / 10 ** d
  const error = pRep <= 0 ? true
    : pComp === "=" ? pRep > round(upP, pDec) || pRep < round(lowP, pDec)
    : pComp === "<" ? pRep < lowP
    : pRep > upP
  // a gross inconsistency (decision error) is an inconsistency where the reported and recalculated p-values fall on
  // opposite sides of alpha. as in statcheck's default, a reported p = .05 counts as significant
  const alpha = 0.05
  const gross = error && (pComp === "=" ? (pRep <= alpha && computed > alpha) || (pRep > alpha && computed <= alpha)
    : pComp === "<" ? pRep <= alpha && computed > alpha
    : pRep >= alpha && computed <= alpha)
  // the test statistic that the reported p-value would require
  const implied = pRep > 0 && pRep < 1 ? invertP(pOf, pRep, type === "r" ? 1 - 1e-12 : null) : null
  return {...parsed, sidedApplies, twoTailed, pOf, mag, step, half, lowStat, upStat, computed, lowP, upP, error, gross, implied}
}
```

```{ojs}
{
  if (scState.message) return html`<div style="color: var(--bs-secondary-color);">${scState.message}</div>`
  const s = scState
  const symbol = statSymbol(s)
  // the horizontal axis runs from zero to beyond both the recalculated and the implied test statistic
  const xMax = s.type === "r" ? 1 : 1.3 * Math.max(s.upStat, s.implied ?? 0, 0.5)
  const shown = [s.lowP, s.pRep, alphaLevel].filter(p => p > 0)
  const yMin = Math.max(1e-15, d3.min(shown) / 5)
  const curve = d3.range(0, 301).map(i => xMax * i / 300).map(x => ({x, p: s.pOf(x)})).filter(d => d.p >= yMin)
  return Plot.plot({
    width, height: Math.min(340, Math.max(260, width * 0.45)), marginLeft: 60, marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 45,
    x: {label: symbol, labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 38, domain: [0, xMax]},
    y: {label: `${s.twoTailed && s.sidedApplies ? "Two-sided " : s.sidedApplies ? "One-sided " : ""}p-value`, labelAnchor: "center", type: "log", domain: [yMin, 1], grid: true, ticks: logTicks(yMin), tickFormat: formatTick},
    style: {fontSize: "13px"},
    marks: [
      Plot.frame({stroke: "currentColor"}),
      // the p-values allowed by a reported inequality
      s.pComp === "<" && s.pRep > yMin ? Plot.rect([{}], {x1: 0, x2: xMax, y1: yMin, y2: s.pRep, fill: "#d9622b", fillOpacity: 0.1}) : null,
      s.pComp === ">" && s.pRep < 1 ? Plot.rect([{}], {x1: 0, x2: xMax, y1: Math.max(s.pRep, yMin), y2: 1, fill: "#d9622b", fillOpacity: 0.1}) : null,
      Plot.ruleY([alphaLevel], {stroke: "currentColor", strokeOpacity: 0.6, strokeDasharray: "2,3"}),
      Plot.text([alphaLevel], {x: xMax, y: d => d, text: () => "α = .05", textAnchor: "end", dx: -4, dy: -7, fillOpacity: 0.7}),
      Plot.line(curve, {x: "x", y: "p", stroke: "currentColor", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      s.pRep > yMin ? Plot.ruleY([s.pRep], {stroke: "#d9622b", strokeWidth: 2}) : null,
      s.implied !== null ? Plot.dot([{x: s.implied, y: s.pRep}], {x: "x", y: "y", fill: "#d9622b", r: 5}) : null,
      s.pRep > yMin ? Plot.text([s.pRep], {x: 0, y: d => d, text: () => `Reported p ${s.pComp} ${s.pText}`, fill: "#d9622b", fontWeight: 600, textAnchor: "start", dx: 6, dy: s.pComp === ">" ? -8 : 9}) : null,
      Plot.ruleX([s.mag], {stroke: "#2780e3", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
      s.computed >= yMin ? Plot.dot([{x: s.mag, y: s.computed}], {x: "x", y: "y", fill: "#2780e3", r: 5}) : null,
      s.computed >= yMin ? Plot.text([{x: s.mag, y: s.computed}], {x: "x", y: "y", text: () => `Recalculated p = ${formatP(s.computed)}`, fill: "#2780e3", fontWeight: 600, textAnchor: "end", dx: -8, dy: 12}) : null
    ]
  })
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  if (scState.message) return html``
  const s = scState
  const symbol = statSymbol(s)
  // zoomed in on the reported test statistic: one and a half units of its last reported decimal on either side
  const xLo = Math.max(0, s.mag - 1.5 * s.step), xHi = s.type === "r" ? Math.min(1, s.mag + 1.5 * s.step) : s.mag + 1.5 * s.step
  const curve = d3.range(0, 201).map(i => xLo + (xHi - xLo) * i / 200).map(x => ({x, p: s.pOf(x)}))
  const [yLo, yHi] = d3.extent(curve, d => d.p)
  const pad = (yHi - yLo) * 0.08
  const domain = [Math.max(0, yLo - pad), yHi + pad]
  const repInside = s.pRep >= domain[0] && s.pRep <= domain[1]
  const where = s.pRep < domain[0] ? "below" : "above"
  return Plot.plot({
    width, height: Math.min(300, Math.max(240, width * 0.4)), marginLeft: 60, marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 45,
    x: {label: `${symbol} (zoomed in on the reported value)`, labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 38, domain: [xLo, xHi]},
    y: {label: "p-value", labelAnchor: "center", domain, grid: true, tickFormat: formatTick},
    style: {fontSize: "13px"},
    marks: [
      Plot.frame({stroke: "currentColor"}),
      // values of the test statistic that round to the reported value, and the p-values they produce
      s.half > 0 ? Plot.rect([{}], {x1: s.lowStat, x2: s.upStat, y1: domain[0], y2: domain[1], fill: "#2780e3", fillOpacity: 0.12}) : null,
      s.half > 0 ? Plot.rect([{}], {x1: xLo, x2: xHi, y1: s.lowP, y2: s.upP, fill: "#2780e3", fillOpacity: 0.12}) : null,
      // the p-values allowed by a reported inequality, where they fall within the plot
      s.pComp === "<" && s.pRep > domain[0] ? Plot.rect([{}], {x1: xLo, x2: xHi, y1: domain[0], y2: Math.min(s.pRep, domain[1]), fill: "#d9622b", fillOpacity: 0.1}) : null,
      s.pComp === ">" && s.pRep < domain[1] ? Plot.rect([{}], {x1: xLo, x2: xHi, y1: Math.max(s.pRep, domain[0]), y2: domain[1], fill: "#d9622b", fillOpacity: 0.1}) : null,
      Plot.line(curve, {x: "x", y: "p", stroke: "currentColor", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      Plot.ruleX([s.mag], {stroke: "#2780e3", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
      Plot.dot([{x: s.mag, y: s.computed}], {x: "x", y: "y", fill: "#2780e3", r: 5}),
      repInside ? Plot.ruleY([s.pRep], {stroke: "#d9622b", strokeWidth: 2}) : null,
      repInside ? Plot.text([s.pRep], {x: xHi, y: d => d, text: () => `Reported p ${s.pComp} ${s.pText}`, fill: "#d9622b", fontWeight: 600, textAnchor: "end", dx: -6, dy: -8}) : null,
      repInside ? null : Plot.text([`Reported p ${s.pComp} ${s.pText} is ${where} this range`], {frameAnchor: where === "below" ? "bottom-right" : "top-right", dx: -8, dy: where === "below" ? -8 : 8, fill: "#d9622b", fontWeight: 600})
    ]
  })
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  if (scState.message) return html``
  const s = scState
  const symbol = statSymbol(s)
  const sided = s.sidedApplies ? (s.twoTailed ? "two-sided " : "one-sided ") : ""
  const reported = `The reported p ${s.pComp} ${s.pText}`
  // bounds of the test statistic, with one more decimal than reported. a correlation has no leading zero, as in APA style
  const bound = x => s.type === "r" ? x.toFixed(s.statDec + 1).replace(/^0/, "") : x.toFixed(s.statDec + 1)
  const range = s.half > 0
    ? `Before rounding, ${symbol} = ${s.statText} could have been anything from ${bound(s.lowStat)} to ${bound(s.upStat)}, which gives a ${sided}p-value between ${formatP(s.lowP)} and ${formatP(s.upP)}.`
    : `Taking ${symbol} = ${s.statText} as exact, the ${sided}p-value is ${formatP(s.computed)}.`
  const implied = s.implied === null ? "" : ` To give ${s.pComp === "=" ? "the reported p-value" : `a p-value of ${s.pText}`}, ${symbol} would have to be about ${s.implied.toFixed(Math.max(2, s.statDec))}.`
  const sidedNote = s.sidedApplies ? "" : ` ${s.type === "F" ? "F" : "χ²"} tests are one-sided by construction, so the first button has no effect on them.`
  const [kind, title, detail] =
    s.pRep <= 0 ? ["bad", "Inconsistent: a p-value cannot be exactly zero.", `statcheck counts a reported p = .000 as an error by default. It would normally be reported as p < .001. ${range}`]
    : !s.error ? ["ok", "Consistent.", `${range} ${reported} is compatible with this.`]
    : !s.gross ? ["warn", "Inconsistent, but the conclusion does not change.", `${range} ${reported} is not compatible with this, but both are on the same side of α = .05.${implied}`]
    : ["bad", "Grossly inconsistent: the conclusion changes.", `${range} ${reported} is not compatible with this, and the reported and recalculated p-values are on opposite sides of α = .05.${implied}`]
  return html`<div class="sb-feedback sb-feedback-${kind}"><strong>${title}</strong> ${detail}${sidedNote}</div>`
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// functions and styles used by the statcheck plot
alphaLevel = 0.05

function parseResult(text) {
  // reads a result reported in APA style, e.g. "t(28) = 2.0, p < .05" or "χ2(1, N = 226) = 6.90, p < .01", and keeps
  // the number of decimals of the test statistic and the p-value, which statcheck needs to account for rounding.
  // returns {message} if the text cannot be read
  const s = String(text).replace(/[−–—]/g, "-").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()
  const m = s.match(/^(t|f|r|z|χ2|χ²|chi2|chi²|x2)\s*(?:\(([^)]*)\))?\s*=\s*(-?\d*\.?\d+)\s*[,;]\s*p\s*([=<>])\s*(\d*\.?\d+)$/i)
  if (!m) return {message: "Type a result in APA style, such as t(28) = 2.0, p < .05. The test can be t, F, r, χ2, or z, and the p-value can be reported with =, <, or >."}
  const type = {t: "t", f: "F", r: "r", z: "z"}[m[1].toLowerCase()] ?? "chi2"
  // degrees of freedom are the plain numbers in the brackets, so that the N in "χ2(1, N = 226)" is left out
  const dfs = (m[2] ?? "").split(",").map(x => x.trim()).filter(x => /^\d*\.?\d+$/.test(x)).map(Number)
  const decimals = x => (x.split(".")[1] ?? "").length
  const stat = Number(m[3]), pRep = Number(m[5])
  const result = {type, stat, statText: m[3], statDec: decimals(m[3]), pComp: m[4], pRep, pText: m[5], pDec: decimals(m[5]), df1: NaN, df2: NaN}
  if (type === "t" || type === "r") result.df2 = dfs[0]
  if (type === "F") { result.df1 = dfs[0]; result.df2 = dfs[1] }
  if (type === "chi2") result.df1 = dfs[0]
  const needs = {t: ["df2"], r: ["df2"], F: ["df1", "df2"], chi2: ["df1"], z: []}[type]
  if (needs.some(k => !(result[k] > 0))) return {message: type === "F" ? "An F test needs two degrees of freedom, e.g. F(2, 40) = 3.50, p = .040." : `This test needs its degrees of freedom in brackets, e.g. ${type === "chi2" ? "χ2(1)" : type + "(28)"}.`}
  if (type === "r" && Math.abs(stat) >= 1) return {message: "A correlation has to be between −1 and 1."}
  if ((type === "F" || type === "chi2") && stat < 0) return {message: "An F or χ2 statistic cannot be negative."}
  if (pRep > 1) return {message: "A p-value cannot be larger than 1."}
  return result
}

function pFrom(type, stat, df1, df2, twoTailed) {
  // the p-value of a test statistic, by the same distributions as statcheck. t and F through the regularised
  // incomplete beta function, chi-squared and z through the regularised upper incomplete gamma function. a z
  // statistic squared is chi-squared with one degree of freedom. a correlation is converted to t first
  let p
  if (type === "t" || type === "r") {
    const t = type === "r" ? stat * Math.sqrt(df2 / (1 - stat * stat)) : stat
    p = betaI(df2 / (df2 + t * t), df2 / 2, 0.5)
  }
  else if (type === "z") p = gammaQ(0.5, stat * stat / 2)
  else if (type === "F") p = stat <= 0 ? 1 : betaI(df2 / (df2 + df1 * stat), df2 / 2, df1 / 2)
  else p = stat <= 0 ? 1 : gammaQ(df1 / 2, stat / 2)
  return (type === "t" || type === "r" || type === "z") && !twoTailed ? p / 2 : p
}

function invertP(pOf, target, upper) {
  // the test statistic whose p-value is target, by bisection: the p-value only decreases as the statistic increases
  let lower = 0
  if (upper === null) { upper = 1; while (pOf(upper) > target && upper < 1e6) upper *= 2 }
  if (pOf(upper) > target) return null
  for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
    const middle = (lower + upper) / 2
    if (pOf(middle) > target) lower = middle; else upper = middle
  }
  return (lower + upper) / 2
}

function statSymbol(s) {
  const symbol = s.type === "chi2" ? "χ²" : s.type
  return s.stat < 0 ? `|${symbol}|` : symbol
}

function formatP(p) {
  // four decimals, without the leading zero, as in APA style; very small values in scientific notation
  if (p === 0) return "0"
  return p < 0.0001 ? p.toExponential(1) : p.toFixed(4).replace(/^0/, "")
}

function logTicks(yMin) {
  // ticks for the logarithmic p-value axis: the conventional thresholds, then every power of ten, or every second one
  // when the axis spans many of them
  const powers = d3.range(3, 16).map(k => 10 ** -k).filter(p => p >= yMin)
  return [1, 0.1, 0.05, 0.01, ...(powers.length > 5 ? powers.filter((p, i) => i % 2 === 1) : powers)].filter(p => p >= yMin)
}

function formatTick(p) {
  return p >= 0.001 ? d3.format("~g")(p).replace(/^0/, "") : d3.format(".0e")(p)
}

function resultInput(examples, initial) {
  // a text box for a reported result, with buttons that fill it with examples. the value is stored on the wrapping
  // div, so that it can be used with viewof
  const input = html`<input type="text" class="form-control sc-input" spellcheck="false" aria-label="Result as reported">`
  input.value = initial
  const view = html`<div class="sc-result">
    <label class="sc-label">Result as reported</label>
    ${input}
    <div class="sb-buttons sc-examples"><span>Examples:</span>${examples.map(e => {
      const button = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto btn-sm">${e}</button>`
      button.onclick = () => {
        input.value = e
        view.value = e
        view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
      }
      return button
    })}</div>
  </div>`
  view.value = initial
  // the input event bubbles up to the wrapping div after this, when the value has already been updated
  input.oninput = () => { view.value = input.value }
  return view
}

function toggleButton(options) {
  // a button that switches between two options ({label, value}) each time it is clicked. it is labelled with what
  // clicking it will change to, which is the option that is not currently in effect. the value is stored on the
  // wrapping div, so that it can be used with viewof. starts on the first option
  let current = 0
  const label = () => { const next = options[(current + 1) % options.length].label; return `Change to ${next.charAt(0).toLowerCase()}${next.slice(1)}` }
  const button = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">${label()}</button>`
  const view = html`<div class="sb-buttons">${button}</div>`
  view.value = options[0].value
  button.onclick = () => {
    current = (current + 1) % options.length
    button.textContent = label()
    view.value = options[current].value
    view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  }
  return view
}

function betaI(x, a, b) {
  // regularised incomplete beta function, by continued fraction
  if (x <= 0) return 0
  if (x >= 1) return 1
  const front = Math.exp(logGamma(a + b) - logGamma(a) - logGamma(b) + a * Math.log(x) + b * Math.log(1 - x))
  const cf = (x, a, b) => {
    let c = 1, d = 1 - (a + b) * x / (a + 1)
    if (Math.abs(d) < 1e-300) d = 1e-300
    d = 1 / d
    let h = d
    for (let m = 1; m < 500; m++) {
      let aa = m * (b - m) * x / ((a + 2 * m - 1) * (a + 2 * m))
      d = 1 + aa * d; if (Math.abs(d) < 1e-300) d = 1e-300
      c = 1 + aa / c; if (Math.abs(c) < 1e-300) c = 1e-300
      d = 1 / d
      h *= d * c
      aa = -(a + m) * (a + b + m) * x / ((a + 2 * m) * (a + 2 * m + 1))
      d = 1 + aa * d; if (Math.abs(d) < 1e-300) d = 1e-300
      c = 1 + aa / c; if (Math.abs(c) < 1e-300) c = 1e-300
      d = 1 / d
      const del = d * c
      h *= del
      if (Math.abs(del - 1) < 1e-14) break
    }
    return h
  }
  return x < (a + 1) / (a + b + 2) ? front * cf(x, a, b) / a : 1 - front * cf(1 - x, b, a) / b
}

function gammaQ(a, x) {
  // regularised upper incomplete gamma function: series for small x, continued fraction otherwise. the upper tail is
  // calculated directly in the continued fraction, so that very small p-values keep their precision
  if (x <= 0) return 1
  const front = Math.exp(-x + a * Math.log(x) - logGamma(a))
  if (x < a + 1) {
    let term = 1 / a, sum = term
    for (let n = 1; n < 500; n++) { term *= x / (a + n); sum += term; if (Math.abs(term) < Math.abs(sum) * 1e-14) break }
    return 1 - sum * front
  }
  let b = x + 1 - a, c = 1e300, d = 1 / b, h = d
  for (let i = 1; i < 500; i++) {
    const an = -i * (i - a)
    b += 2
    d = an * d + b; if (Math.abs(d) < 1e-300) d = 1e-300
    c = b + an / c; if (Math.abs(c) < 1e-300) c = 1e-300
    d = 1 / d
    const del = d * c
    h *= del
    if (Math.abs(del - 1) < 1e-14) break
  }
  return front * h
}

function logGamma(x) {
  // Lanczos approximation
  const c = [76.18009172947146, -86.50532032941677, 24.01409824083091, -1.231739572450155, 0.001208650973866179, -0.000005395239384953]
  let y = x, sum = 1.000000000190015
  for (const cj of c) sum += cj / ++y
  return -(x + 5.5) + (x + 0.5) * Math.log(x + 5.5) + Math.log(2.5066282746310005 * sum / x)
}

statcheckPlotStyle = html`<style>
  .sb-buttons { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; }
  .sb-feedback { margin: 0.5rem 0 1.5rem; padding: 0.6rem 0.9rem; border-left: 4px solid; background: rgba(128, 128, 128, 0.08); }
  .sb-feedback-ok { border-color: #3b9c6e; }
  .sb-feedback-warn { border-color: #d9a02b; }
  .sb-feedback-bad { border-color: #c0392b; }
  .sc-label { font-weight: 600; display: block; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; }
  .sc-input { font-size: 1.15rem; max-width: 28rem; }
  .sc-examples { margin: 0.5rem 0 0.75rem; font-size: 0.9rem; }
  .sc-examples .btn { font-family: var(--bs-font-monospace); }
</style>`
```

#### Simple calculator for effect size plausibility

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof smdInput = {
  const fields = [["study", "Study"], ["m1", "Group 1 mean"], ["sd1", "Group 1 SD"], ["n1", "Group 1 n"], ["m2", "Group 2 mean"], ["sd2", "Group 2 SD"], ["n2", "Group 2 n"]]
  // the study in the table above, and a set of four hypothetical studies to show several at once
  const examples = {
    "This study": [["Example", 11.2, 4.9, 64, 25.1, 4.1, 64]],
    "Four studies": [["A", 22.1, 5.2, 40, 24.3, 5.5, 41], ["B", 3.8, 1.1, 25, 4.4, 1.2, 25], ["C", 14.2, 0.9, 64, 17.1, 1.0, 64], ["D", 3.6, 1.2, 10, 4.9, 1.3, 10]]
  }
  const body = html`<tbody></tbody>`
  const addRow = (values = []) => {
    const tr = html`<tr></tr>`
    tr.inputs = fields.map(([key, label], j) => {
      const input = html`<input type="text" class="form-control form-control-sm" inputmode="${j === 0 ? "text" : "decimal"}" aria-label="${label}">`
      input.value = values[j] ?? ""
      input.onpaste = e => paste(e, tr, j)
      return input
    })
    const remove = html`<button class="btn btn-sm smd-remove" title="Remove this row" aria-label="Remove this row">×</button>`
    remove.onclick = () => { tr.remove(); if (body.children.length === 0) addRow() }
    tr.append(...tr.inputs.map(input => html`<td>${input}</td>`), html`<td>${remove}</td>`)
    body.append(tr)
    return tr
  }
  // a block of cells copied from a spreadsheet (tab-separated) or typed as comma-separated values fills the grid
  // from the cell it was pasted into, adding rows as needed. a single value is pasted as normal
  const paste = (e, tr, j) => {
    const text = e.clipboardData.getData("text").replace(/\r/g, "").replace(/\n+$/, "")
    if (!/[\t\n,]/.test(text)) return
    e.preventDefault()
    let row = tr
    for (const line of text.split("\n")) {
      const cells = line.split(line.includes("\t") ? "\t" : ",")
      cells.forEach((cell, k) => { if (j + k < fields.length) row.inputs[j + k].value = cell.trim() })
      row = row.nextElementSibling ?? addRow()
    }
    // a trailing empty row that was only added for the next line is removed again
    if (row !== tr && row.inputs.every(input => input.value === "") && row.previousElementSibling) row.remove()
  }
  const load = rows => { body.replaceChildren(); rows.forEach(values => addRow(values)) }
  load(examples["This study"])
  const exampleButtons = Object.entries(examples).map(([name, rows]) => {
    const button = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">${name}</button>`
    button.onclick = () => load(rows)
    return button
  })
  const measure = html`<select class="form-select form-select-sm smd-measure" aria-label="Effect size">
    <option value="g">Cohen's d with Hedges' correction</option>
    <option value="d">Cohen's d without Hedges' correction</option>
  </select>`
  const add = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Add row</button>`
  const clear = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Clear all</button>`
  const run = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Calculate SMDs</button>`
  add.onclick = () => addRow().inputs[0].focus()
  clear.onclick = () => { body.replaceChildren(); addRow().inputs[0].focus() }
  const view = html`<div>
    <div class="sb-buttons sc-examples smd-examples"><span>Examples:</span>${exampleButtons}</div>
    <div class="table-responsive"><table class="table table-sm smd-grid">
      <thead>
        <tr><th rowspan="2">Study</th><th colspan="3">Group 1 (e.g., intervention)</th><th colspan="3">Group 2 (e.g., control)</th><th rowspan="2"></th></tr>
        <tr><th><em>M</em></th><th><em>SD</em></th><th><em>n</em></th><th><em>M</em></th><th><em>SD</em></th><th><em>n</em></th></tr>
      </thead>
      ${body}
    </table></div>
    <div class="smd-controls"><label class="sc-label">Effect size</label>${measure}</div>
    <div class="sb-buttons">${add}${clear}${run}</div>
  </div>`
  // the value only changes when the calculate button is clicked
  view.value = {runs: 0}
  run.onclick = () => {
    const rows = [...body.children].map(tr => Object.fromEntries(fields.map(([key], j) => [key, tr.inputs[j].value.trim()])))
    view.value = {runs: view.value.runs + 1, rows, correct: measure.value === "g"}
    view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  }
  return view
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```
```{ojs}
// functions and styles used by the SMD calculator

function smdChecked(rows) {
  // reads the values in each row of the grid. rows that are entirely empty are left out. a row is only sent to R if all
  // six values are numbers, both SDs are above zero, and both sample sizes are whole numbers of at least 2
  return rows.map((r, i) => ({...r, row: i + 1}))
    .filter(r => Object.values(r).some(v => v !== "" && typeof v === "string"))
    .map(r => {
      const values = Object.fromEntries(["m1", "sd1", "n1", "m2", "sd2", "n2"].map(k => [k, r[k] === "" ? NaN : Number(r[k])]))
      const problem = Object.values(values).some(v => !Number.isFinite(v)) ? "Missing or non-numeric values"
        : values.sd1 <= 0 || values.sd2 <= 0 ? "SDs must be above zero"
        : !Number.isInteger(values.n1) || !Number.isInteger(values.n2) || values.n1 < 2 || values.n2 < 2 ? "Sample sizes must be whole numbers of at least 2"
        : null
      return {...r, ...values, study: r.study || `Row ${r.row}`, valid: problem === null, problem}
    })
}

async function runEscalc(rows, correct) {
  const {webR, rVersion, version} = await webRSession.load("metafor")
  const valid = rows.filter(r => r.valid)
  const shelter = await new webR.Shelter()
  try {
    // the values are passed to R as numeric vectors, never pasted into the code
    const col = k => valid.map(r => r[k])
    const res = await shelter.evalR(`
      es <- summary(escalc(measure = "SMD", m1i = m1, sd1i = sd1, n1i = n1, m2i = m2, sd2i = sd2, n2i = n2, correct = correct))
      data.frame(yi = as.numeric(es$yi), vi = as.numeric(es$vi), sei = es$sei, ci.lb = es$ci.lb, ci.ub = es$ci.ub)
    `, {env: {m1: col("m1"), sd1: col("sd1"), n1: col("n1"), m2: col("m2"), sd2: col("sd2"), n2: col("n2"), correct}})
    const out = await res.toD3()
    valid.forEach((r, i) => Object.assign(r, out[i]))
    return {rows, correct, runAt: new Date(), metaforVersion: version, rVersion}
  } finally {
    shelter.purge()
  }
}

function smdResults(run) {
  const {rows, correct, metaforVersion, rVersion} = run
  const name = correct ? "Cohen's d with Hedges' correction" : "Cohen's d without Hedges' correction"
  const valid = rows.filter(r => r.valid)
  const f2 = x => x.toFixed(2).replace("-", "−")
  // labels for the plot: the study names, with the row number added where two rows have the same name
  const counts = d3.rollup(valid, v => v.length, r => r.study)
  valid.forEach(r => { r.label = counts.get(r.study) > 1 ? `${r.study} (row ${r.row})` : r.study })
  const extent = d3.extent([0, ...valid.flatMap(r => [r["ci.lb"], r["ci.ub"]])])
  const plot = Plot.plot({
    width, height: 70 + 34 * valid.length, marginLeft: Math.min(200, 20 + 7 * d3.max(valid, r => r.label.length)), marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 45,
    x: {label: `${name}, with 95% CI`, labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 38, grid: true, nice: true, domain: extent},
    y: {label: null, domain: valid.map(r => r.label), padding: 0.5, tickSize: 0},
    style: {fontSize: "13px"},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "currentColor", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeOpacity: 0.6}),
      Plot.link(valid, {x1: "ci.lb", x2: "ci.ub", y1: "label", y2: "label", stroke: "#2780e3", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      // marker area in proportion to the total sample size, as in a forest plot
      Plot.dot(valid, {x: "yi", y: "label", fill: "#2780e3", symbol: "square", r: r => 3 + 5 * Math.sqrt((r.n1 + r.n2) / d3.max(valid, v => v.n1 + v.n2))})
    ]
  })
  const body = rows.map(r => r.valid
    ? html`<tr><td>${r.row}</td><td>${r.study}</td><td>${r.n1}</td><td>${r.n2}</td><td>${f2(r.yi)}</td><td>${r.sei.toFixed(3)}</td><td>[${f2(r["ci.lb"])}, ${f2(r["ci.ub"])}]</td></tr>`
    : html`<tr class="sc-row-none"><td>${r.row}</td><td>${r.study}</td><td colspan="5">Not calculated: ${r.problem}</td></tr>`)
  return html`<div>
    <div class="table-responsive"><table class="table table-sm smd-table">
      <thead><tr><th>Row</th><th>Study</th><th><em>n</em><sub>1</sub></th><th><em>n</em><sub>2</sub></th><th><em>d</em></th><th><em>SE</em></th><th>95% CI</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>${body}</tbody>
    </table></div>
    ${plot}
    <div class="sc-status">${name} for group 1 minus group 2, calculated by <code>escalc(measure = "SMD"${correct ? "" : ", correct = FALSE"})</code> with metafor ${metaforVersion}, ${rVersion}, running in webR ${webrVersion}. The confidence intervals are the estimate ± 1.96 standard errors. The values were taken as exact, with no allowance for rounding.</div>
    <div class="sb-buttons sc-download">${smdDownloadButton(run)}</div>
  </div>`
}

function smdDownloadButton(run) {
  // the inputs, escalc's output, and the versions used, one row per row of the grid that was not empty
  const {rows, correct, runAt, metaforVersion, rVersion} = run
  const columns = ["row", "study", "m1", "sd1", "n1", "m2", "sd2", "n2", "measure", "yi", "vi", "sei", "ci_lb", "ci_ub", "status",
    "metafor_version", "r_version", "webr_version", "run_at"]
  const settings = {measure: correct ? "Cohen's d with Hedges' correction (escalc measure = SMD)" : "Cohen's d without Hedges' correction (escalc measure = SMD, correct = FALSE)", metafor_version: metaforVersion, r_version: rVersion, webr_version: webrVersion, run_at: runAt.toISOString()}
  const records = rows.map(r => r.valid
    ? {...r, ci_lb: r["ci.lb"], ci_ub: r["ci.ub"], status: "Calculated", ...settings}
    // rows that were not calculated keep the values as they were entered
    : {...r, ...Object.fromEntries(["m1", "sd1", "n1", "m2", "sd2", "n2"].map(k => [k, Number.isFinite(r[k]) ? r[k] : ""])), status: `Not calculated: ${r.problem}`, ...settings})
  return csvDownloadButton(columns, records, "smd_results", runAt)
}

smdCalculatorStyle = html`<style>
  .smd-examples .btn { font-family: inherit; }
  .smd-grid { font-size: 0.9rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; }
  .smd-grid th { text-align: center; font-weight: 600; border-bottom-width: 1px; }
  .smd-grid td { padding: 0.15rem; }
  .smd-grid td:first-child input { min-width: 6rem; }
  .smd-grid input { min-width: 4rem; text-align: right; background: transparent; color: inherit; }
  .smd-grid td:first-child input { text-align: left; }
  .smd-remove { line-height: 1; padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; color: var(--bs-secondary-color); }
  .smd-controls { margin: 0.5rem 0 0.75rem; max-width: 24rem; }
  .smd-table { font-size: 0.9rem; margin-top: 0.75rem; }
  .smd-table td:nth-child(n+3), .smd-table th:nth-child(n+3) { text-align: right; }
  .smd-table .sc-row-none td { text-align: left; }
</style>`
```

#### Forensic recalculator that takes rounding into account {#sec-smd-calculator}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof ttInput = {
  const examples = {
    "This study": {groups: [["11.2", "4.9", "64"], ["25.1", "4.1", "64"]], pOp: "less_than", p: ".001", d: "−3.06", lower: "−3.57", upper: "−2.55"},
    "Inconsistent CI": {groups: [["10.30", "3.12", "50"], ["8.71", "2.80", "48"]], pOp: "less_than", p: ".01", d: "0.53", lower: "0.20", upper: "0.90"}
  }
  const field = label => html`<input type="text" class="form-control form-control-sm" inputmode="decimal" aria-label="${label}">`
  const groups = [1, 2].map(g => ({m: field(`Group ${g} mean`), sd: field(`Group ${g} SD`), n: field(`Group ${g} n`)}))
  const pOp = html`<select class="form-select form-select-sm tt-op" aria-label="How the p-value was reported">
    <option value="equals">=</option><option value="less_than">&lt;</option><option value="greater_than">&gt;</option>
  </select>`
  const p = field("Reported p-value"), d = field("Reported SMD"), lower = field("Lower bound of the reported 95% CI"), upper = field("Upper bound of the reported 95% CI")
  const alternative = html`<select class="form-select form-select-sm" aria-label="Test">
    <option value="two.sided">Two-sided</option>
    <option value="one.sided">One-sided, in the direction of the difference</option>
  </select>`
  const direction = html`<select class="form-select form-select-sm" aria-label="Difference">
    <option value="m1_minus_m2">Group 1 minus group 2</option>
    <option value="m2_minus_m1">Group 2 minus group 1</option>
    <option value="both">Either</option>
  </select>`
  const seConfusion = html`<input type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" id="tt-se">`
  const load = ex => {
    ex.groups.forEach((values, i) => ["m", "sd", "n"].forEach((k, j) => groups[i][k].value = values[j]))
    pOp.value = ex.pOp; p.value = ex.p; d.value = ex.d; lower.value = ex.lower; upper.value = ex.upper
  }
  load(examples["This study"])
  const exampleButtons = Object.entries(examples).map(([name, ex]) => {
    const button = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">${name}</button>`
    button.onclick = () => load(ex)
    return button
  })
  const clear = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Clear all</button>`
  const run = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Check</button>`
  clear.onclick = () => {
    for (const input of [...groups.flatMap(g => [g.m, g.sd, g.n]), p, d, lower, upper]) input.value = ""
    groups[0].m.focus()
  }
  const view = html`<div>
    <div class="sb-buttons sc-examples smd-examples"><span>Examples:</span>${exampleButtons}</div>
    <div class="table-responsive"><table class="table table-sm smd-grid tt-grid">
      <thead><tr><th></th><th><em>M</em></th><th><em>SD</em></th><th><em>n</em></th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>${groups.map((g, i) => html`<tr><td class="tt-label">${i === 0 ? "Group 1 (e.g., intervention)" : "Group 2 (e.g., control)"}</td><td>${g.m}</td><td>${g.sd}</td><td>${g.n}</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
    </table></div>
    <div class="tt-reported">
      <label><span>Reported <em>p</em> (optional)</span><span class="tt-pair">${pOp}${p}</span></label>
      <label><span>Reported SMD (optional)</span>${d}</label>
      <label><span>95% CI lower (optional)</span>${lower}</label>
      <label><span>95% CI upper (optional)</span>${upper}</label>
    </div>
    <div class="sg-controls">
      <label><span>Test</span>${alternative}</label>
      <label><span>Difference</span>${direction}</label>
    </div>
    <div class="form-check sc-option">${seConfusion}<label class="form-check-label" for="tt-se">The values after the means might be standard errors rather than <em>SD</em>s</label></div>
    <div class="sb-buttons">${clear}${run}</div>
  </div>`
  // the value only changes when the check button is clicked
  view.value = {runs: 0}
  run.onclick = () => {
    view.value = {
      runs: view.value.runs + 1,
      groups: groups.map(g => ({m: g.m.value.trim(), sd: g.sd.value.trim(), n: g.n.value.trim()})),
      pOp: pOp.value, p: p.value.trim(), d: d.value.trim(), lower: lower.value.trim(), upper: upper.value.trim(),
      alternative: alternative.value, direction: direction.value, seConfusion: seConfusion.checked
    }
    view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  }
  return view
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// functions and styles used by the t-test calculator

function ttChecked(raw) {
  // reads and checks the values in the calculator. the means and SDs are required. the number of decimal places of each
  // kind of value is taken from the values as typed, and if they differ the fewest is used, which is the most lenient
  const problems = []
  const clean = s => s.replace(/−/g, "-")
  const number = s => /^[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)$/.test(clean(s)) ? Number(clean(s)) : NaN
  const decimals = s => s.match(/\.(\d*)$/)?.[1].length ?? 0
  const groups = raw.groups.map((g, i) => {
    const out = {m: number(g.m), sd: number(g.sd), n: number(g.n)}
    if (!Number.isFinite(out.m)) problems.push(`Group ${i + 1}: enter its mean.`)
    if (!Number.isFinite(out.sd) || out.sd <= 0) problems.push(`Group ${i + 1}: its SD must be a number above zero.`)
    if (!Number.isInteger(out.n) || out.n < 2) problems.push(`Group ${i + 1}: its n must be a whole number of at least 2.`)
    return out
  })
  const optional = (s, label) => {
    if (s === "") return null
    const x = number(s)
    if (!Number.isFinite(x)) problems.push(`The reported ${label} is not a number.`)
    return x
  }
  const p = optional(raw.p, "p-value"), d = optional(raw.d, "SMD"), lower = optional(raw.lower, "lower bound of the CI"), upper = optional(raw.upper, "upper bound of the CI")
  if (p !== null && (p < 0 || p > 1)) problems.push("The reported p-value must be between 0 and 1.")
  if ((lower === null) !== (upper === null)) problems.push("Enter both bounds of the CI, or neither.")
  else if (lower !== null && lower >= upper) problems.push("The lower bound of the CI must be smaller than its upper bound.")
  const fewest = values => d3.min(values.filter(v => v !== ""), decimals)
  return {
    problems, groups, p, d, lower, upper, raw,
    mDigits: fewest(raw.groups.map(g => g.m)), sdDigits: fewest(raw.groups.map(g => g.sd)),
    pDigits: p === null ? null : decimals(raw.p),
    dDigits: d === null && lower === null ? null : fewest([raw.d, raw.lower, raw.upper]),
    pOp: raw.pOp, alternative: raw.alternative === "one.sided" ? oneSided(groups, raw.direction) : ["two.sided"],
    direction: raw.direction, seConfusion: raw.seConfusion,
    slow: raw.direction === "both" && raw.seConfusion
  }
}

function oneSided(groups, direction) {
  // a reported one-sided p-value is almost always in the direction of the observed difference. including the other
  // direction too would allow p-values close to 1, and make almost any reported p-value consistent. when either
  // difference is allowed, both tails are needed, because recalc applies each alternative to both differences
  if (direction === "both") return ["less", "greater"]
  const diff = direction === "m1_minus_m2" ? groups[0].m - groups[1].m : groups[1].m - groups[0].m
  return [diff >= 0 ? "greater" : "less"]
}

async function runTTest(input) {
  const {webR, rVersion, recalcVersion} = await recalcR.get()
  const shelter = await new webR.Shelter()
  try {
    // the values are passed to R as vectors, never pasted into the code. values that were not entered are passed as
    // NaN, which R turns into NULL
    const none = [NaN], opt = x => x === null ? none : [x]
    const [g1, g2] = input.groups
    const res = await shelter.evalR(`
      opt <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NULL else x
      res <- recalc_env$recalc_independent_t(
        m1 = m1, m2 = m2, sd1 = sd1, sd2 = sd2, n1 = n1, n2 = n2,
        m_digits = m_digits, sd_digits = sd_digits, rounding = "either",
        p = opt(p), p_digits = opt(p_digits), p_operator = p_operator, alternative = alternative,
        d = opt(d), d_ci_lower = opt(lower), d_ci_upper = opt(upper), d_digits = opt(d_digits),
        direction = direction, include_se_sd_confusion = se_confusion)
      list(reproduced = as.data.frame(res$reproduced), p = res$p_method_intervals,
           d = res$d_method_intervals, ci = res$ci_method_intervals)
    `, {env: {
      m1: g1.m, m2: g2.m, sd1: g1.sd, sd2: g2.sd, n1: g1.n, n2: g2.n, m_digits: input.mDigits, sd_digits: input.sdDigits,
      p: opt(input.p), p_digits: opt(input.pDigits), p_operator: input.pOp, alternative: input.alternative,
      d: opt(input.d), lower: opt(input.lower), upper: opt(input.upper), d_digits: opt(input.dDigits),
      direction: input.direction, se_confusion: input.seConfusion
    }})
    const part = async name => (await res.get(name)).toD3()
    const [reproduced] = await part("reproduced")
    return {input, reproduced, pMethods: await part("p"), dMethods: await part("d"), ciMethods: await part("ci"),
      recalcVersion, rVersion, runAt: new Date()}
  } finally {
    shelter.purge()
  }
}

function ttResults(run) {
  const {input, reproduced: r} = run
  const blue = "#2780e3", orange = "#d9622b"
  const dd = input.dDigits ?? 2
  const fmtD = x => x.toFixed(dd + 1).replace("-", "−")
  const superscript = n => `${n < 0 ? "⁻" : ""}${[...String(Math.abs(n))].map(c => "⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹"[c]).join("")}`
  const fmtP = x => x < 0.001 ? x.toExponential(1).replace(/e([-+])(\d+)/, (m, s, e) => ` × 10${superscript(s === "-" ? -e : +e)}`) : x.toFixed(4).replace(/^0\./, ".")
  const range = (lo, hi, f) => !Number.isFinite(lo) || !Number.isFinite(hi) ? "" : `${f(lo)} to ${f(hi)}`
  const verdict = ok => ok === null || ok === undefined ? ["Not checked", "na"] : ok ? ["Consistent", "ok"] : ["Inconsistent", "bad"]
  const badge = ([label, kind]) => html`<span class="sc-verdict sc-verdict-${kind}">${label}</span>`
  const opSymbol = {equals: "=", less_than: "<", greater_than: ">"}[input.pOp]
  const rows = [
    {label: html`<em>p</em>`, reported: input.p === null ? "" : `${opSymbol} ${input.raw.p}`, range: range(r.min_p, r.max_p, fmtP), ok: r.p_inbounds},
    {label: "SMD", reported: input.raw.d, range: range(r.min_d, r.max_d, fmtD), ok: r.d_inbounds},
    {label: "95% CI, lower bound", reported: input.raw.lower, range: range(r.min_ci_lower, r.max_ci_lower, fmtD), ok: r.ci_lower_inbounds},
    {label: "95% CI, upper bound", reported: input.raw.upper, range: range(r.min_ci_upper, r.max_ci_upper, fmtD), ok: r.ci_upper_inbounds},
    {label: "95% CI, both bounds", reported: input.lower === null ? "" : `[${input.raw.lower}, ${input.raw.upper}]`, range: "from a single combination of choices", ok: r.ci_inbounds}
  ]

  // plain-language names for the analytic choices, leaving out those that are the same for every method shown
  const names = {
    p: [{student_t: "Student's t", welch_t: "Welch's t"}, {"two.sided": "two-sided", less: "one-sided (less)", greater: "one-sided (greater)"}, {m1_minus_m2: "1 − 2", m2_minus_m1: "2 − 1"}, {sd: "as SDs", se_converted: "SDs from SEs"}],
    d: [{pooled_df: "pooled SD (df)", pooled_n: "pooled SD (N)", simple_avg: "average variance"}, {none: "no correction", approx: "Hedges (approx.)", exact: "Hedges (exact)"}, {m1_minus_m2: "1 − 2", m2_minus_m1: "2 − 1"}, {sd: "as SDs", se_converted: "SDs from SEs"}]
  }
  const label = (methods, map) => {
    const parts = methods.map(m => m.method.split("|"))
    const varies = map.map((_, k) => new Set(parts.map(p => p[k])).size > 1)
    methods.forEach((m, i) => { m.label = parts[i].map((code, k) => varies[k] ? (map[k][code] ?? code) : null).filter(x => x).join(", ") || "All" })
    return methods
  }
  const pMethods = label(run.pMethods.map(m => ({...m, lower: m.p_min, upper: m.p_max})), names.p)
  const dMethods = label(run.dMethods.map(m => ({...m, lower: m.d_min, upper: m.d_max})), names.d)

  // the CI is summarised by CI method and SE formula: each row covers every denominator and Hedges correction, and is
  // marked if any combination within it produces both reported bounds
  const ciNames = {wald_t: "Wald t", wald_z: "Wald z", welch_t: "Welch t", nct: "noncentral t"}
  const seNames = {hedges_olkin: "Hedges–Olkin SE", cumming: "Cumming SE", uncorrected: "simple SE", none: ""}
  const ciGroups = d3.groups(run.ciMethods, m => m.method.split("|").slice(4).join("|")).map(([key, ms]) => {
    const [ci, se] = key.split("|")
    return {label: [ciNames[ci] ?? ci, seNames[se] ?? se].filter(x => x).join(", "), lowerMin: d3.min(ms, m => m.ci_lower_min), lowerMax: d3.max(ms, m => m.ci_lower_max),
      upperMin: d3.min(ms, m => m.ci_upper_min), upperMax: d3.max(ms, m => m.ci_upper_max), fits: ms.some(m => m.ci_inbounds === true)}
  })
  ciGroups.forEach(g => { if (input.lower !== null && g.fits) g.label += " ✓" })

  const ulpBand = (value, digits) => [value - 0.5 * 10 ** -digits, value + 0.5 * 10 ** -digits]
  const height = n => 40 + 24 * n
  const marginLeft = methods => Math.min(260, 20 + 6.5 * d3.max(methods, m => m.label.length))
  const pPlot = () => {
    const lo = d3.min([...pMethods.map(m => m.lower), input.p ?? 1]), hi = d3.max([...pMethods.map(m => m.upper), input.p ?? 0])
    const domain = [Math.max(lo / 5, 1e-300), Math.min(1, hi * 5)]
    // ticks at powers of ten, at most about eight of them, or also at 2 and 5 times them when the range is narrow.
    // labelled .001 and so on, or with powers of ten below that
    const exponents = d3.range(Math.floor(Math.log10(domain[0])), Math.ceil(Math.log10(domain[1])) + 1)
    const within = v => v >= domain[0] && v <= domain[1]
    const powers = exponents.map(e => 10 ** e).filter(within)
    const step = Math.ceil(powers.length / 8)
    const ticks = powers.length >= 3 ? powers.filter((v, i) => (powers.length - 1 - i) % step === 0)
      : exponents.flatMap(e => [1, 2, 5].map(k => k * 10 ** e)).filter(within)
    const tickFormat = v => {
      const e = Math.floor(Math.log10(v) + 1e-9), k = Math.round(v / 10 ** e)
      return e >= -3 ? String(+v.toPrecision(1)).replace(/^0\./, ".") : `${k === 1 ? "" : `${k} × `}10${superscript(e)}`
    }
    const reported = input.p === null ? [] : input.pOp === "equals" ? [ulpBand(input.p, input.pDigits)]
      : input.pOp === "less_than" ? [[domain[0], input.p]] : [[input.p, domain[1]]]
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: height(pMethods.length), marginLeft: marginLeft(pMethods), marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 35,
      x: {type: "log", domain, ticks, tickFormat, label: "p-value (log scale)", labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 30, grid: true},
      y: {domain: pMethods.map(m => m.label), label: null, tickSize: 0, padding: 0.3},
      style: {fontSize: "12px"},
      marks: [
        Plot.rectX(reported, {x1: d => d[0], x2: d => d[1], fill: orange, fillOpacity: 0.25}),
        Plot.link(pMethods, {x1: "lower", x2: "upper", y1: "label", y2: "label", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 8}),
        Plot.dot(pMethods, {x: "lower", y: "label", fill: blue, r: 4})
      ]
    })
  }
  const dPlot = () => Plot.plot({
    width, height: height(dMethods.length), marginLeft: marginLeft(dMethods), marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 35,
    x: {label: "SMD", labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 30, grid: true, nice: true},
    y: {domain: dMethods.map(m => m.label), label: null, tickSize: 0, padding: 0.3},
    style: {fontSize: "12px"},
    marks: [
      input.d === null ? null : Plot.rectX([ulpBand(input.d, dd)], {x1: d => d[0], x2: d => d[1], fill: orange, fillOpacity: 0.35}),
      Plot.link(dMethods, {x1: "lower", x2: "upper", y1: "label", y2: "label", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 8}),
      Plot.dot(dMethods, {x: "lower", y: "label", fill: blue, r: 4})
    ]
  })
  const ciPlot = () => Plot.plot({
    width, height: height(ciGroups.length), marginLeft: marginLeft(ciGroups), marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 35,
    x: {label: "95% CI of the SMD", labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 30, grid: true, nice: true},
    y: {domain: ciGroups.map(g => g.label), label: null, tickSize: 0, padding: 0.3},
    style: {fontSize: "12px"},
    marks: [
      input.lower === null ? null : Plot.rectX([ulpBand(input.lower, dd), ulpBand(input.upper, dd)], {x1: d => d[0], x2: d => d[1], fill: orange, fillOpacity: 0.35}),
      Plot.link(ciGroups, {x1: "lowerMin", x2: "lowerMax", y1: "label", y2: "label", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 8}),
      Plot.link(ciGroups, {x1: "upperMin", x2: "upperMax", y1: "label", y2: "label", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 8})
    ]
  })

  return html`<div>
    <div class="table-responsive"><table class="table table-sm sg-table">
      <thead><tr><th></th><th>Reported</th><th>Recalculated</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>${rows.map(row => html`<tr><td>${row.label}</td><td>${row.reported || "–"}</td><td>${row.range}</td><td>${badge(verdict(row.ok))}</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
    </table></div>
    <div class="sg-plot"><div class="sg-plot-title"><em>p</em>-value, by test</div>${pPlot()}</div>
    <div class="sg-plot"><div class="sg-plot-title">SMD, by how it was calculated</div>${dPlot()}</div>
    <div class="sg-plot"><div class="sg-plot-title">95% CI of the SMD, by how it was calculated</div>${ciPlot()}</div>
    <div class="sc-status">Each blue bar is the range of values that one way of calculating the result produces across the rounding of the means and <em>SD</em>s, and orange is the reported value, as the range of values that round to it (or, for <em>p</em> &lt; and <em>p</em> &gt;, the values it allows). In the CI plot, the two bars in each row are the ranges of the lower and upper bounds, across every denominator and Hedges' correction, and ✓ marks the rows in which a single combination of choices produces both reported bounds.</div>
    <div class="sc-status">Calculated by <code>recalc_independent_t()</code> from recalc ${run.recalcVersion} (commit <a href="https://github.com/ianhussey/recalc/tree/${recalcCommit}">${recalcCommit.slice(0, 7)}</a>), ${run.rVersion}, running in webR ${webrVersion}. Means were taken as rounded to ${input.mDigits} decimal place${input.mDigits === 1 ? "" : "s"}, <em>SD</em>s to ${input.sdDigits}${input.pDigits === null ? "" : `, the p-value to ${input.pDigits}`}${input.dDigits === null ? "" : `, and the SMD and its CI to ${input.dDigits}`}.</div>
    <div class="sb-buttons sc-download">${ttDownloadButton(run, rows, verdict)}</div>
  </div>`
}

function ttDownloadButton(run, rows, verdict) {
  // the inputs, the verdicts, and the settings and versions used, one row per check
  const {input, recalcVersion, rVersion, runAt} = run
  const [g1, g2] = input.raw.groups
  const columns = ["check", "reported", "recalculated", "verdict", "m1", "sd1", "n1", "m2", "sd2", "n2", "p_operator", "alternative",
    "direction", "se_sd_confusion", "m_digits", "sd_digits", "p_digits", "d_digits", "recalc_version", "recalc_commit", "r_version", "webr_version", "run_at"]
  const common = {m1: g1.m, sd1: g1.sd, n1: g1.n, m2: g2.m, sd2: g2.sd, n2: g2.n, p_operator: input.pOp, alternative: input.alternative.join(" or "),
    direction: input.direction, se_sd_confusion: input.seConfusion, m_digits: input.mDigits, sd_digits: input.sdDigits, p_digits: input.pDigits ?? "",
    d_digits: input.dDigits ?? "", recalc_version: recalcVersion, recalc_commit: recalcCommit, r_version: rVersion, webr_version: webrVersion, run_at: runAt.toISOString()}
  const plain = x => x instanceof Node ? x.textContent : x
  const records = rows.map(row => ({check: plain(row.label), reported: row.reported, recalculated: row.range, verdict: verdict(row.ok)[0], ...common}))
  return csvDownloadButton(columns, records, "t_test_results", runAt)
}

ttCalculatorStyle = html`<style>
  .tt-grid td.tt-label { font-size: 0.85rem; vertical-align: middle; white-space: nowrap; padding-right: 0.75rem; }
  .tt-grid { max-width: 34rem; }
  .tt-reported { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-end; gap: 0.75rem 1rem; margin: 0.5rem 0; }
  .tt-reported label { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.2rem; font-size: 0.85rem; flex: 0 1 10rem; min-width: 8rem; }
  .tt-reported label > span:first-child { white-space: nowrap; }
  .tt-pair { display: flex; gap: 0.25rem; }
  .tt-pair .tt-op { flex: 0 0 3.5rem; }
</style>`
```

### ORs from cell counts

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof orInput = {
  const examples = {
    "Ayahuasca: hospitalisations": {groups: ["Ayahuasca", "Placebo"], outcome: "Hospitalised", cells: [["4", "11"], ["0", "15"]]},
    "Escitalopram: suicidal ideation": {groups: ["Escitalopram", "Placebo"], outcome: "Suicidal ideation", cells: [["13", "123"], ["2", "135"]]}
  }
  const field = (label, numeric = true) => html`<input type="text" class="form-control form-control-sm" inputmode="${numeric ? "numeric" : "text"}" aria-label="${label}">`
  const names = [field("Name of group 1", false), field("Name of group 2", false)]
  const cells = [0, 1].map(i => [field(`Group ${i + 1} with the event`), field(`Group ${i + 1} without the event`)])
  const outcome = html`<span class="or-outcome"></span>`
  const pOp = html`<select class="form-select form-select-sm tt-op" aria-label="How the p-value was reported">
    <option value="equals">=</option><option value="less_than">&lt;</option><option value="greater_than">&gt;</option>
  </select>`
  const p = field("Reported p-value"), or = field("Reported odds ratio"), lower = field("Lower bound of the reported 95% CI"), upper = field("Upper bound of the reported 95% CI")
  for (const input of [p, or, lower, upper]) input.inputMode = "decimal"
  const load = ex => {
    ex.groups.forEach((name, i) => names[i].value = name)
    ex.cells.forEach((row, i) => row.forEach((v, j) => cells[i][j].value = v))
    outcome.textContent = ex.outcome
    for (const input of [p, or, lower, upper]) input.value = ""
  }
  load(Object.values(examples)[0])
  const exampleButtons = Object.entries(examples).map(([name, ex]) => {
    const button = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">${name}</button>`
    button.onclick = () => load(ex)
    return button
  })
  const clear = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Clear all</button>`
  const run = html`<button class="btn btn-quarto">Check</button>`
  clear.onclick = () => {
    for (const input of [...names, ...cells.flat(), p, or, lower, upper]) input.value = ""
    outcome.textContent = ""
    names[0].focus()
  }
  const view = html`<div>
    <div class="sb-buttons sc-examples smd-examples"><span>Examples:</span>${exampleButtons}</div>
    <div class="table-responsive"><table class="table table-sm smd-grid or-grid">
      <thead><tr><th>Group</th><th>With the event${html`<br>`}${outcome}</th><th>Without the event</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>${[0, 1].map(i => html`<tr><td>${names[i]}</td><td>${cells[i][0]}</td><td>${cells[i][1]}</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
    </table></div>
    <div class="tt-reported">
      <label><span>Reported OR (optional)</span>${or}</label>
      <label><span>95% CI lower (optional)</span>${lower}</label>
      <label><span>95% CI upper (optional)</span>${upper}</label>
      <label><span>Reported <em>p</em> (optional)</span><span class="tt-pair">${pOp}${p}</span></label>
    </div>
    <div class="sb-buttons">${clear}${run}</div>
  </div>`
  // the value only changes when the check button is clicked
  view.value = {runs: 0}
  run.onclick = () => {
    view.value = {
      runs: view.value.runs + 1,
      names: names.map(n => n.value.trim()), cells: cells.map(row => row.map(c => c.value.trim())),
      pOp: pOp.value, p: p.value.trim(), or: or.value.trim(), lower: lower.value.trim(), upper: upper.value.trim()
    }
    view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  }
  return view
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// functions and styles used by the odds ratio calculator

function orChecked(raw) {
  // reads and checks the values in the calculator. the counts must be whole numbers, and each group must have at least
  // one participant. the number of decimal places of the OR and its CI is taken from the values as typed, the fewest if
  // they differ
  const problems = []
  const clean = s => s.replace(/−/g, "-")
  const number = s => /^[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)$/.test(clean(s)) ? Number(clean(s)) : NaN
  const decimals = s => s.match(/\.(\d*)$/)?.[1].length ?? 0
  const names = raw.names.map((n, i) => n || `Group ${i + 1}`)
  const cells = raw.cells.map((row, i) => row.map((c, j) => {
    const x = number(c)
    if (!Number.isInteger(x) || x < 0) problems.push(`${names[i]}: the number ${j === 0 ? "with" : "without"} the event must be a whole number of 0 or more.`)
    return x
  }))
  cells.forEach((row, i) => { if (row.every(Number.isInteger) && row[0] + row[1] === 0) problems.push(`${names[i]}: the group has no participants.`) })
  const optional = (s, label) => {
    if (s === "") return null
    const x = number(s)
    if (!Number.isFinite(x)) problems.push(`The reported ${label} is not a number.`)
    return x
  }
  const p = optional(raw.p, "p-value"), or = optional(raw.or, "odds ratio"), lower = optional(raw.lower, "lower bound of the CI"), upper = optional(raw.upper, "upper bound of the CI")
  if (p !== null && (p < 0 || p > 1)) problems.push("The reported p-value must be between 0 and 1.")
  if ([or, lower, upper].some(x => x !== null && x <= 0)) problems.push("An odds ratio and its CI must be above zero.")
  if (lower !== null && upper !== null && lower >= upper) problems.push("The lower bound of the CI must be smaller than its upper bound.")
  const fewest = values => d3.min(values.filter(v => v !== ""), decimals)
  return {
    problems, names, cells, p, or, lower, upper, raw, pOp: raw.pOp,
    pDigits: p === null ? null : decimals(raw.p),
    orDigits: or === null && lower === null && upper === null ? null : fewest([raw.or, raw.lower, raw.upper])
  }
}

async function runOddsRatio(input) {
  const {webR, rVersion, recalcVersion} = await recalcR.get()
  const shelter = await new webR.Shelter()
  try {
    // the values are passed to R as vectors, never pasted into the code. values that were not entered are passed as
    // NaN, which R turns into NULL. the counts are in row order: group 1 with and without the event, then group 2
    const none = [NaN], opt = x => x === null ? none : [x]
    const res = await shelter.evalR(`
      opt <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NULL else x
      res <- recalc_env$recalc_oddsratio(
        counts = counts, n_rows = 2, n_cols = 2,
        odds_ratio = opt(or), or_ci_lower = opt(lower), or_ci_upper = opt(upper),
        or_digits = if (is.null(opt(or_digits))) 2L else as.integer(or_digits),
        p = opt(p), p_digits = opt(p_digits), p_operator = p_operator)
      list(reproduced = as.data.frame(res$reproduced), p = as.data.frame(res$method_intervals), or = as.data.frame(res$or_results))
    `, {env: {
      counts: input.cells.flat(), or: opt(input.or), lower: opt(input.lower), upper: opt(input.upper), or_digits: opt(input.orDigits),
      p: opt(input.p), p_digits: opt(input.pDigits), p_operator: input.pOp
    }})
    const part = async name => (await res.get(name)).toD3()
    const [reproduced] = await part("reproduced")
    return {input, reproduced, pMethods: await part("p"), orRows: await part("or"), recalcVersion, rVersion, runAt: new Date()}
  } finally {
    shelter.purge()
  }
}

function orResults(run) {
  const {input, reproduced: r} = run
  const blue = "#2780e3", orange = "#d9622b"
  const finite = x => typeof x === "number" && Number.isFinite(x)
  const od = input.orDigits ?? 2
  const fmtOR = x => x.toFixed(od + 1)
  const superscript = n => `${n < 0 ? "⁻" : ""}${[...String(Math.abs(n))].map(c => "⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹"[c]).join("")}`
  const fmtP = x => x < 0.001 ? x.toExponential(1).replace(/e([-+])(\d+)/, (m, s, e) => ` × 10${superscript(s === "-" ? -e : +e)}`) : x.toFixed(4).replace(/^0\./, ".")
  const range = (values, f) => { const v = values.filter(finite); return v.length === 0 ? "cannot be calculated" : d3.min(v) === d3.max(v) ? f(v[0]) : `${f(d3.min(v))} to ${f(d3.max(v))}` }
  // with a zero count, some CI methods have no finite upper limit, which recalc returns as NA
  const unbounded = values => values.some(v => !finite(v)) ? (values.some(finite) ? ", or no finite limit" : "no finite limit") : ""
  const verdict = ok => ok === null || ok === undefined ? ["Not checked", "na"] : ok ? ["Consistent", "ok"] : ["Inconsistent", "bad"]
  const badge = ([label, kind]) => html`<span class="sc-verdict sc-verdict-${kind}">${label}</span>`
  const opSymbol = {equals: "=", less_than: "<", greater_than: ">"}[input.pOp]

  // the table and plots show the OR of group 1 relative to group 2. the verdicts also accept the reciprocal
  const asIs = run.orRows.filter(o => o.orientation === "as_is")
  const corrected = asIs.some(o => o.cc_label !== "cc:none")
  const rows = [
    {label: html`OR (${input.names[0]} vs ${input.names[1]})`, reported: input.raw.or, range: asIs.some(o => finite(o.or_unrounded)) ? range(asIs.map(o => o.or_unrounded), fmtOR) + (asIs.some(o => !finite(o.or_unrounded)) ? ", or infinite" : "") : "infinite", ok: r.or_inbounds},
    {label: "95% CI, lower bound", reported: input.raw.lower, range: range(asIs.map(o => o.ci_lower_unrounded), fmtOR), ok: r.or_ci_lower_inbounds},
    {label: "95% CI, upper bound", reported: input.raw.upper, range: asIs.some(o => finite(o.ci_upper_unrounded)) ? range(asIs.map(o => o.ci_upper_unrounded), fmtOR) + unbounded(asIs.map(o => o.ci_upper_unrounded)) : unbounded(asIs.map(o => o.ci_upper_unrounded)), ok: r.or_ci_upper_inbounds},
    {label: html`<em>p</em>`, reported: input.p === null ? "" : `${opSymbol} ${input.raw.p}`, range: range([r.min_p, r.max_p], fmtP), ok: r.p_inbounds}
  ]

  const testNames = {pearson: "Pearson χ²", yates: "χ², Yates' correction", n1_chisq: "χ², N − 1", likelihood_ratio: "likelihood ratio", wald_z: "Wald z",
    fisher: "Fisher's exact", fisher_central: "Fisher's exact, central", fisher_midp: "Fisher's mid-p", fisher_midp_sas: "Fisher's mid-p (SAS)"}
  const estimatorNames = {uncond_mle: "sample OR", cond_mle: "conditional MLE"}
  const ciNames = {wald_logor: "Wald, log scale", cornfield_exact: "exact", midp_exact: "mid-p exact", profile_likelihood: "profile likelihood"}
  const pMethods = run.pMethods.filter(m => finite(m.p_min)).map(m => ({label: testNames[m.method] ?? m.method, lower: m.p_min, upper: m.p_max}))
  // every estimator and CI method keeps its row, so that the rows do not change from one table to another. those with
  // no finite value, which happens when a count is zero, are marked instead of drawn
  const estimates = d3.groups(asIs, o => o.estimator).map(([e, os]) => {
    const v = os.map(o => o.or_unrounded).filter(finite)
    return {label: estimatorNames[e] ?? e, lower: d3.min(v), upper: d3.max(v), open: v.length === 0}
  })
  const cis = d3.groups(asIs, o => o.ci_method).map(([m, os]) => {
    const lo = os.map(o => o.ci_lower_unrounded).filter(finite), hi = os.map(o => o.ci_upper_unrounded).filter(finite)
    return {label: ciNames[m] ?? m, lowerMin: d3.min(lo), lowerMax: d3.max(lo), upperMin: d3.min(hi), upperMax: d3.max(hi), open: hi.length < os.length}
  })

  const height = n => 40 + 24 * n
  const marginLeft = items => Math.min(220, 20 + 6.5 * d3.max(items, m => m.label.length))
  const logTicks = domain => {
    // ticks at powers of ten, or also at 2 and 5 times them when the range is narrow
    const exponents = d3.range(Math.floor(Math.log10(domain[0])), Math.ceil(Math.log10(domain[1])) + 1)
    const within = v => v >= domain[0] && v <= domain[1]
    const powers = exponents.map(e => 10 ** e).filter(within)
    const step = Math.ceil(powers.length / 8)
    return powers.length >= 3 ? powers.filter((v, i) => (powers.length - 1 - i) % step === 0) : exponents.flatMap(e => [1, 2, 5].map(k => k * 10 ** e)).filter(within)
  }
  const tickFormat = v => { const e = Math.floor(Math.log10(v) + 1e-9), k = Math.round(v / 10 ** e); return e >= -3 ? String(+v.toPrecision(1)).replace(/^0\./, ".") : `${k === 1 ? "" : `${k} × `}10${superscript(e)}` }
  const ulpBand = (value, digits) => [value - 0.5 * 10 ** -digits, value + 0.5 * 10 ** -digits]
  const logPlot = (items, label, reported, bars) => {
    const values = [...items.flatMap(bars), ...reported.flat()].filter(v => finite(v) && v > 0)
    const domain = [d3.min(values) / 2, d3.max(values) * 2]
    // a lower bound of exactly 0 cannot be drawn on a log scale, so it is drawn at the left edge
    const clip = v => Math.max(v, domain[0])
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: height(items.length), marginLeft: marginLeft(items), marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 35,
      x: {type: "log", domain, ticks: logTicks(domain), tickFormat, label, labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 30, grid: true},
      y: {domain: items.map(m => m.label), label: null, tickSize: 0, padding: 0.3},
      style: {fontSize: "12px"},
      marks: [
        Plot.rectX(reported, {x1: d => d[0], x2: d => d[1], fill: orange, fillOpacity: 0.3}),
        ...(items[0] && "lowerMin" in items[0]
          ? [Plot.link(items.filter(m => finite(m.lowerMin)), {x1: m => clip(m.lowerMin), x2: m => clip(m.lowerMax), y1: "label", y2: "label", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 8}),
             Plot.dot(items.filter(m => finite(m.lowerMin)), {x: m => clip(m.lowerMin), y: "label", fill: blue, r: 4}),
             Plot.link(items.filter(m => finite(m.upperMin)), {x1: "upperMin", x2: "upperMax", y1: "label", y2: "label", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 8}),
             Plot.dot(items.filter(m => finite(m.upperMin)), {x: "upperMin", y: "label", fill: blue, r: 4}),
             Plot.text(items.filter(m => m.open), {x: domain[1], y: "label", text: () => "no upper limit →", textAnchor: "end", fill: blue, fontSize: 11})]
          : [Plot.link(items.filter(m => finite(m.lower)), {x1: m => clip(m.lower), x2: m => clip(m.upper), y1: "label", y2: "label", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 8}),
             Plot.dot(items.filter(m => finite(m.lower)), {x: m => clip(m.lower), y: "label", fill: blue, r: 4}),
             Plot.text(items.filter(m => m.open), {x: domain[1], y: "label", text: () => "infinite →", textAnchor: "end", fill: blue, fontSize: 11})])
      ]
    })
  }
  const pReported = input.p === null ? [] : input.pOp === "equals" ? [ulpBand(input.p, input.pDigits)] : input.pOp === "less_than" ? [[1e-300, input.p]] : [[input.p, 1]]
  const orReported = input.or === null ? [] : [ulpBand(input.or, od)]
  const ciReported = [input.lower, input.upper].filter(x => x !== null).map(x => ulpBand(x, od))

  return html`<div>
    <div class="table-responsive"><table class="table table-sm sg-table">
      <thead><tr><th></th><th>Reported</th><th>Recalculated</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>${rows.map(row => html`<tr><td>${row.label}</td><td>${row.reported || "–"}</td><td>${row.range}</td><td>${badge(verdict(row.ok))}</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
    </table></div>
    ${corrected ? html`<div class="sc-status sg-note">One of the counts is zero, so the odds in one group are zero and the OR is infinite (or zero, with the groups the other way round). The sample OR can only be calculated after adding 0.5 to every cell, as was done here. The conditional estimate stays infinite, and the exact, mid-p, and profile likelihood intervals have no finite upper limit.</div>` : ""}
    <div class="sg-plot"><div class="sg-plot-title"><em>p</em>-value, by test</div>${logPlot(pMethods, "p-value (log scale)", pReported, m => [m.lower, m.upper])}</div>
    ${estimates.some(m => !m.open) ? html`<div class="sg-plot"><div class="sg-plot-title">Odds ratio, by estimator</div>${logPlot(estimates, "odds ratio (log scale)", orReported, m => [m.lower, m.upper])}</div>` : ""}
    ${cis.some(c => finite(c.lowerMin)) ? html`<div class="sg-plot"><div class="sg-plot-title">95% CI of the odds ratio, by method</div>${logPlot(cis, "odds ratio (log scale)", ciReported, m => [m.lowerMin, m.lowerMax, m.upperMin, m.upperMax])}</div>` : ""}
    <div class="sc-status">Blue is what each method produces from the counts, and orange is the reported value, as the range of values that round to it (or, for <em>p</em> &lt; and <em>p</em> &gt;, the values it allows). In the CI plot, each row has the lower and the upper bound, across both estimators. The OR is that of ${input.names[0]} relative to ${input.names[1]}; a reported OR or CI is also counted as consistent if it matches with the groups the other way round.</div>
    <div class="sc-status">Calculated by <code>recalc_oddsratio()</code> from recalc ${run.recalcVersion} (commit <a href="https://github.com/ianhussey/recalc/tree/${recalcCommit}">${recalcCommit.slice(0, 7)}</a>), ${run.rVersion}, running in webR ${webrVersion}. The counts were taken as exact${input.orDigits === null ? "" : `, the OR and its CI as rounded to ${input.orDigits} decimal place${input.orDigits === 1 ? "" : "s"}`}${input.pDigits === null ? "" : `, and the p-value to ${input.pDigits}`}.</div>
    <div class="sb-buttons sc-download">${orDownloadButton(run, rows, verdict)}</div>
  </div>`
}

function orDownloadButton(run, rows, verdict) {
  // the inputs, the verdicts, and the settings and versions used, one row per check
  const {input, recalcVersion, rVersion, runAt} = run
  const columns = ["check", "reported", "recalculated", "verdict", "group1", "group1_event", "group1_no_event", "group2", "group2_event", "group2_no_event",
    "p_operator", "or_digits", "p_digits", "recalc_version", "recalc_commit", "r_version", "webr_version", "run_at"]
  const common = {group1: input.names[0], group1_event: input.raw.cells[0][0], group1_no_event: input.raw.cells[0][1],
    group2: input.names[1], group2_event: input.raw.cells[1][0], group2_no_event: input.raw.cells[1][1], p_operator: input.pOp,
    or_digits: input.orDigits ?? "", p_digits: input.pDigits ?? "", recalc_version: recalcVersion, recalc_commit: recalcCommit, r_version: rVersion,
    webr_version: webrVersion, run_at: runAt.toISOString()}
  const plain = x => x instanceof Node ? x.textContent : x
  return csvDownloadButton(columns, rows.map(row => ({check: plain(row.label), reported: row.reported, recalculated: row.range, verdict: verdict(row.ok)[0], ...common})), "odds_ratio_results", runAt)
}

orCalculatorStyle = html`<style>
  .or-grid { max-width: 34rem; }
  .or-grid td:first-child input { min-width: 9rem; text-align: left; }
  .or-outcome { font-weight: 400; font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--bs-secondary-color); }
</style>`
```
